citation.sourceDocument: USDA FNA SNAP Fiscal Year 2026 Cost-of-Living Adjustments (48 contiguous states and DC), Table 1, effective Oct 1, 2025
citation.sourceNote: SNAP runs on the FEDERAL FISCAL year, not the calendar year, so these figures are effective October 1, 2025 through September 30, 2026 — the one dataset here whose clock differs from every other. The maximum allotments derive from USDA's Thrifty Food Plan and rise irregularly with household size rather than by a fixed increment, which is why they are stored as a table; above eight people, add $218 per person. The benefit is not the allotment: it is the maximum allotment minus 30% of net income (the expected contribution), floored at a $24 minimum for one- and two-person households. Net income is gross income minus the standard deduction and 20% of earned income. Eligibility runs on two tests, gross income at or below 130% of the poverty line and net income at or below 100%. This shard covers the 48 CONTIGUOUS STATES AND DC only; Alaska, Hawaii, Guam and the U.S. Virgin Islands have their own, higher allotments and are not seeded. Omitted: the excess shelter deduction (often the largest deduction a household has, and capped except for elderly or disabled members), the dependent-care, medical and child-support deductions, the asset limits, broad-based categorical eligibility (which many states use to waive the gross-income test), the ABAWD work requirements, and the state options that vary all of this. The figure is an estimate of the maximum a household could receive, not an eligibility determination. Every figure here was verified against Table 1 of the USDA COLA page on 2026-08-29. The August audit could not read the allotments and recorded them as standing as authored; it was reading the per-fiscal-year page, which renders its tables client-side, while the COLA index one level up states them in the markup. All eight household sizes and the $218 each-additional-member amount match. Note the agency renamed itself the Food and Nutrition Administration on June 1, 2026, and fns.usda.gov now redirects to fna.usda.gov.
